correctness.rationale: Each proper named three-colouring corresponds to a cyclic sign word of total increment zero modulo three and one of three start colours. Richness and rich-neighbor domination yield exactly the four-sign local transfer condition. Closed 24-state walks count each sign word three times; hence the trace identity. Integer Newton identities produce the exact stated characteristic polynomial. Strong connectivity and 3-/5-cycles make the matrix primitive; a simple positive golden-ratio eigenvalue is uniquely dominant by the factorization and Perron–Frobenius. The standard-library checker verifies connectivity, exact polynomial, and direct counts n=3..10; independent sign-word enumeration n=3..18 also matched. Unproved limits: none for the stated graph domain; bibliographic priority is separate.

value.rationale: Counting all optimal named colorings of natural graphs is a motivated refinement of an existence theorem. The exact 24-state integer trace works for arbitrary cycle length, the factorization gives an explicit linear recurrence, and the limiting count has the golden ratio as a non-obvious growth constant. The proportion among all proper 3-colorings decays exponentially rather than staying bounded away from zero. It is not a renamed chromatic-index fact, a finite-table recomputation or an arbitrary parameter slice; it treats every cycle. This is a self-contained exact enumerative statement without claiming a larger graph-family classification.
